packs.title: Big Days, Small Discoveries
packs.promise: Find a personal story, a playful experiment and a slower detail inside Pigeon Forge’s big attractions.

q.s: Follow one human story through the museum.
st: Enter with your valid ticket and choose one passenger or crew story from the actual interpretation. Let that person guide your visit rather than rushing to every display.

Collect three different details: a piece of ordinary life, a choice or difficulty during the voyage, and something the museum explains about that person’s outcome. Use the displayed account; leave an unknown detail unknown.
After the visit, write a three-sentence portrait in your own words. End with the detail you most want to remember.

q.s: Make a tiny scene of your own.
st: Find an available wax-figure scene that interests you. Read who it represents before choosing a pose; you do not have to know the celebrity already.
Observe the figure’s gesture. Create a contrasting response of your own: serious beside playful, still beside energetic, or another pair you choose.
Save an optional photo or describe the two gestures and invent a one-line scene title. Keep your title clearly your own, rather than a quotation from the person.

q.s: Bring home a memory after the curtain.
st: Arrive for your booked show and follow staff seating instructions. Put away your recording devices for this task and enjoy the actual production.
Choose three moments to remember: a sound, a movement and a change of atmosphere. You do not need to remember a performer’s name or a particular stunt.
After leaving the performance area, write three short lines that recreate those moments in your own words. Share your favorite with a companion, or keep it for yourself.

packs.title: Mill to Island
packs.promise: Follow craft, river and playful wheels between Old Mill Square and The Island.

q.s: Find three ways a grain becomes a meal.
st: Find a displayed grain product and read its actual label without opening a package.
Collect three food connections from the shelves: a grain or flour, a prepared mix, and something you might serve with the finished dish.
Write a tiny menu that uses your three finds. Make clear which dish is your own idea rather than a recipe promised by the shop.

q.s: Borrow a palette from handmade pottery.
st: Browse the visitor display and choose three glaze colors on actual pieces. Observe without handling fragile stock unless staff invite it.
Connect each color with something you have seen outdoors: stream, stone, sky, bark or your own choice.
Sketch a simple vessel or describe it, then name a new three-color glaze of your own. Keep your invention separate from the maker’s actual product names.

q.s: Turn a fountain performance into a little score.
st: Find a safe open viewing position outside the basin and clear of the main walkway. Wait for the next operating fountain performance.
Choose three changes in height, grouping or rhythm. Represent them as three drawn marks or three short words in sequence.
Add an original title to your tiny score. Finish here, then allow your planned return time to Patriot Park or your onward destination.
